citeAs: Amini, A., Gabriel, S., Lin, S., Koncel-Kedziorski, R., Choi, Y., & Hajishirzi, H. (2019). MathQA: Towards Interpretable Math Word Problem Solving with Operation-Based Formalisms. arXiv preprint arXiv:1905.13319.
creator: Aida Amini, Saadia Gabriel, Shanchuan Lin, Rik Koncel-Kedziorski, Yejin Choi, Hannaneh Hajishirzi (University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI)
description: A large-scale dataset of 37k English multiple-choice math word problems densely annotated with operation programs.
name: MathQA
rai:annotatorDemographics: High-quality crowd workers on Figure Eight.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: At least 2 out of 3 validators should rank the operation program as valid for it to be selected. The validation accuracy is 94.64% across categories. Expert evaluation of 500 problems shows 92% of annotations are valid, with 87% agreement between expert validation and crowd sourcing validation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotators are provided with a problem description, a list of operations related to the problem category, and a list of valid arguments. They iteratively select operations and arguments until the problem is solved. The platform only accepts programs which include some numbers from the problem, and whose final calculation is very close to the correct numeric solution.
rai:dataCollection: Problems from the AQuA dataset were categorized into math domains using term frequencies, and then crowd workers annotated them with formal operation programs.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: AQuA dataset (Ling et al., 2017), which provides over 100K GRE- and GMAT-level math word problems.
rai:dataLimitations: Some problems are not solvable given current math word problem solving frameworks because they require a level of reasoning not yet modeled by neural networks (e.g., sequence problems).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Annotations were expanded to cover more problems from the AQuA dataset by finding closely similar problems (using Levenshtein distance with a threshold of 4 words) and replacing numeric values with generic numbers.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Math problems are first categorized into math domains using term frequencies. These domains are used to prune the search space of possible operations to align with the word problem text.
rai:dataUseCases: Training deep-learning models to solve math word problems.

null_reasons.rai:dataBiases: No explicit discussion of data biases.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data handling.
null_reasons.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Automatic annotations were experimented with but not included in the final dataset; only crowdsourced annotations were used.
